label: Containment in every cause from the strict comparative and more-such-has-the-perfection (inference)
rule: Excluded middle on c = x; strict comparative then more-such-has-the-perfection
meaning: Excluded middle decides whether the cause c is x itself. If it is, x's being in act in r is c's. If not, the strict comparative (STMT-CAUSE-OF-QUALITY-IN-ANOTHER-IS-MORE-SUCH) makes c more r than x (MORE_1), and STMT-MORE-SUCH-HAS-THE-PERFECTION gives that c is in act in r. Together with the previous argument this factors the existing four-premise derivation PERFECTION-PREEXISTENCE-FROM-CAUSAL-TRANSFER through respect-wise containment: the containment premise is the hinge between the Aristotelian comparative pair and q.4 a.2. All premises except excluded middle stay open.
